# AgentOS Kernel

You are running with a persistent second brain stored in this repo at `brain/`.
Your sandbox may be ephemeral. **Git is the disk.** Nothing you learn survives a
session unless it is committed and pushed.

This file is the kernel. It is deliberately small: it contains no knowledge, only
the instruction to go get knowledge. It is harness-agnostic — it assumes nothing
about your model, your vendor, or your tooling beyond `bash`, `git`, and `python3`.

## Boot — first tool call of every session, no exceptions

```bash
bash bin/os boot
```

That one command prints working memory, open loops, and the lessons ledger. Do it
before answering anything, even "hi". A session that skips boot starts amnesiac and
will confidently tell the user there is no prior context — which is false; the
context is one command away.

If boot fails, say so plainly. Do not improvise a memory you do not have.

## Save — last tool call of every session

```bash
bash bin/os save "<one-line summary of this session>"
```

`save` regenerates the dashboard, commits `brain/` + `docs/`, and pushes. Run it
after any durable decision too, not only at the end. An unpushed insight is a lost
insight.

## Write-back rules

During the work, not after:

| What happened | Command |
|---|---|
| Learned a durable fact, preference, or gotcha | `bin/os lesson "When X → do Y. Because Z."` |
| Made a decision with a tradeoff | `bin/os decide "<title>"`, then fill the file |
| Finished a chunk of work | `bin/os log "..."` |
| New concept worth linking | `bin/os note "<Title>"`, link it with `[[wikilinks]]` |
| Working on a loop | tick the ledger in `brain/loops/<name>.md` as you go |
| Need to find something | `bin/os recall "<term>"` |

Working memory lives in `brain/STATE.md`. Keep it under ~60 lines: it is loaded on
every single boot. Anything colder belongs in `brain/wiki/` and gets recalled on
demand, not carried in context.

## The three vault layers

Capture flows inward. Nothing is born a wiki note.

| Layer | Holds | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `brain/raw/` | unprocessed capture — clippings, transcripts, dumps | append freely, never cite directly |
| `brain/wiki/` | atomic, wikilinked, one-idea-per-note knowledge | rewritten in place, never duplicated |
| `brain/output/` | shipped artifacts — posts, reports, drafts | immutable once shipped |

Promote `raw` → `wiki` by distilling, not copying. Promote `wiki` → `output` by
composing. If you find yourself citing a `raw/` file as though it were knowledge,
stop and write the note first.

## Loops

Multi-session work runs as a **loop**, never as a conversation you hope to
remember. `bin/os loop next <name>` gives you the next unchecked step plus the
loop's fixed goal. Do exactly that step, tick it, `save`, and stop. Fresh context
each iteration is the point — the ledger remembers, you don't.

Two rules keep loops honest:

1. **Steps must be externally verifiable.** "Fix auth" is not a step. "Extract
   `verifyToken` into `src/auth/token.ts`, tests still pass" is.
2. **Two identical failures ends the loop.** Write the blocker into `# Notes` and
   escalate. A third identical attempt produces confident garbage.

## Precedence

Explicit user instruction > this kernel > `brain/lessons.md` > habit.

If a lesson is now wrong, edit or delete it. A stale brain is worse than no brain.

## Harness independence

This OS binds to any agent that can run a shell command. The kernel you are reading
lives in `AGENTS.md`; harness-specific bindings are generated from it by
`adapters/install.sh` and are disposable. Never write logic into a harness binding —
write it here or in `bin/os`, and let the adapter point at it.

If your harness supports session hooks, wire them to the same `bin/os boot` and
`bin/os save` entry points. One runtime, many loaders, no duplicated logic.
